description:
The fixture-generation scripts in pkix-ct/tests/fixtures/sct-oracle/ implement a layered oracle design that should be defended:

1. Each gen_*.py script builds the wire-format bytes from RFC text WITHOUT calling into pkix-ct.
2. Each script self-cross-checks: e.g., `gen_precert_entry_sct.py` strips the SCT-list extension TWICE (once via cryptography's CertificateBuilder, once via a hand-rolled DER walker) and asserts equality.
3. Each script verifies signatures via openssl in a subprocess BEFORE committing the fixture.
4. Rust tests then assert pkix-ct's reconstruction matches the committed fixture byte-for-byte.

This satisfies AGENTS.md non-negotiable 'No test may use the code under test as its own oracle' with three layers of redundancy. A future contributor might suggest 'simplifying' by replacing the Python oracle with a Rust fixture generator that uses pkix-ct's own encoder for the byte layout. That would collapse all three layers into self-validation and is exactly what the test-integrity rule forbids.

Also defend: the live-log fixture (PKIX-baac.8) adds a real CT log's STH + inclusion proof, exercising the full pipeline against bytes that pkix-ct's authors did not control. This is the strongest possible end-to-end test for SCT verification — keep it.
title: Layered independent-oracle test design (oracle self-test + openssl cross-check + Rust assertion)
